379 N Morrison Ave, San Jose, CA

claims.note: Early development; plans to use SB 330.
Stated as up to 100. The article's mix (28 studios, 54 one-beds, 54 two-beds) adds to 136.

City file PRE26-106 (Enhanced Preliminary Review, filed 2026-04-10): demolish a single-family house and an office building for a mixed-use building with 3,000 sq ft of ground-floor commercial and 138 residential units.
Enhanced Preliminary Review for the 138-unit mixed-use building; status Complete.
2022 General Plan Amendment (Mixed Use Commercial to Transit Residential), conforming rezoning (LI to TR) and General Plan text amendment; environmental review ER22-062.

construction_notes.text: Article says the effort is led by a team of individuals rather than a development company; no developer named.

City files GP22-008 and C22-023 changed the 0.46-gross-acre site from Mixed Use Commercial to Transit Residential and rezoned it from LI to TR. GPT22-005 added the Transit Residential designation to The Alameda Urban Village Plan, with a minimum 0.50 commercial FAR, and raised the height limit from 55 to 85 feet. The 2023 CEQA filing states no development was proposed at that time.

Earlier city preliminary reviews on APN 261-02-053: PRE19-174 (Urban Tech Development, applicant Gustavo Auqui), a 7-story building with ground-floor office, second-floor parking and five residential floors; PRE21-083 (applicant Anthony Ho, LPMD Architects), a 9-story hotel of about 154 rooms.

Unit counts differ by source: SF YIMBY (June 2026) reports up to 100 units with a mix of 28 studios, 54 one-bedrooms and 54 two-bedrooms (136 in total); city file PRE26-106 (April 2026) describes 138 units.
